A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same metalens-based depth-estimation system. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite renaming, reorganization and substantial additions.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulated benchmark results, a 42-scene physical evaluation, component and few-shot ablations, and measured metalens responses.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds DfD comparisons, controlled ablations, backbone-transfer experiments, moving-object demonstrations and numerical PSF analyses.

M1.justification: The polarization-to-pseudo-RGB mapping, rotating-PSF design, DPT fine-tuning objectives and simulator procedure are retained. v2 Appendix E and v3 Appendix H contain matching soft-slicing, compositing and background-completion equations and Algorithm 1. Renaming 'PSF splatting' and testing additional optical scales or backbones do not establish a changed core method.

E1.justification: v3 adds FlyingThings3D evaluation at a 1–5 m optical operating range and simulated and physical moving-object sequences testing temporal depth consistency. NYU Depth V2, MPI Sintel, Hypersim and MIT-CGH-4K already appeared in v2; their redistribution between the main text and appendices is not additional coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds Depth Anything v3 and MoGe v2 to the NYU, MIT-CGH-4K and physical comparisons. Table 3 newly benchmarks DeepDfD and Split-Aperture, which v2 cited without evaluating. Appendix I also introduces comparisons against double-helix and conventional-lens PSFs.

E3.justification: The new DfD protocol uses a 5-mm-diameter metalens, 50-mm focal length, 1–5 m range, capacity-matched Small backbone, and log10 and delta1 metrics. New controls vary optics, architecture, pretraining and inclusion of real training data. For retained 100-sample benchmarks, v2 Appendix A.1 specifies validation splits whereas v3 Appendix D.1 specifies test splits; this is a reported setting revision without evidence establishing reruns.

E4.justification: v3 adds controlled optics/architecture/pretraining and input-fusion ablations, CKA feature analysis, backbone transfer, motion consistency, and photon-budget, edge-orientation and PSF-ambiguity analyses. Its sim-to-real ablations test components with and without real training data. Conversely, v2 Table 3's one- and three-real-sample sensitivity results are removed.

E5.justification: v3 newly states that average physical-label uncertainty is below 1 cm; v2 only describes approximate labels and their error sources. The retained benchmark tables use unchanged mean-and-standard-deviation reporting. Neither version specifies a repeated-run, seed or significance-testing protocol.

E6.justification: Substantial new results accompany the DfD comparisons, ablations, backbone transfer and PSF analyses. v3 Table 3 reports MAE 0.022 for Ours-Small versus 0.089 for DeepDfD and 0.086 for Split-Aperture. Physical Ours-Base results change from MAE/L1 0.0344 and RMSE 0.0810 to 0.032 and 0.089 in Table 2. The four retained appendix benchmark tables have identical numerical entries across versions.

T1.justification: New Appendix I introduces a Poisson observation model with background, Fisher information and Cramer–Rao bounds for depth and joint depth–edge-orientation estimation, plus inverse-problem conditioning arguments. This substantially expands the formal analysis beyond v2's diffraction and rotating-PSF derivations, which remain in v3 Appendix J.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains passive, single-shot metric depth estimation combining a metalens with pretrained depth priors. v3 extends the abstract, introduction and conclusion's performance claim to competing depth-from-defocus methods, broadening the claim beyond v2's monocular-model comparisons without replacing the principal research contribution.

C2.justification: v3 develops explanations separating pretrained-prior benefits from architecture and optical-design effects, and interpreting feature preservation and PSF noise robustness. Section 5 adds specific limitations involving photon throughput, longer exposures, polarization-dependent sampling and noise, and high-frequency imbalance from reflections or polarized illumination. These substantially extend v2's discussion of field of view, depth range, tube length and approximate labels.

D1.justification: v3 supplies technical details for new comparisons, including two-channel decoder-fusion input, the scaled optics' 1.7 m focus distance, double-helix rotation, and photon/background settings. The original fabrication instructions, sensor specifications, training hyperparameters, A100 hardware and training-time disclosure are retained.

R1.justification: Research positioning shifts substantially toward computational optics, DfD, dual-pixel and birefractive imaging. v3 adds discussion and citations including PS2F and defocus-based Marigold, and distinguishes its simulator from earlier alpha-compositing approaches. Stereo-matching and Gaussian-splatting references and their associated motivation are removed.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'Wavefront Prompting' to 'Wavefront Encoding,' and substantial passages in the abstract, related work, input adaptation and simulator explanation are rewritten. Experiments are reorganized around monocular-model versus DfD comparisons, and the appendix structure expands and reorganizes the original material.

P2.justification: v3 changes the document from two-column to single-column layout and extensively rearranges figures and tables. It adds input-compatibility and disocclusion panels, feature-similarity plots, new comparison and ablation tables, motion sequences, and CRLB/correlation figures. Existing benchmark displays are also relocated and reformatted.

improvement.justification: Direct DfD comparisons and controlled optics, architecture and pretraining ablations address important gaps in v2's comparative evidence and attribution of gains. Appendix I strengthens the optical rationale, while Section 5 gives substantially clearer practical limitations. These benefits outweigh the removal of one-/three-shot sensitivity results and isolated reporting problems, notably v3 Table 7's real-data RMSE of 0.0096 below its MAE of 0.0348. The improvement primarily concerns evidential support and explanation, rather than a changed core method.
